text.p: U.S. farmers will use the new "Freedom to Farm" law to plant 68.800 million acres of soybeans, the most since 1980, and 81.416 million acres of corn, the highest since 1985, the Agriculture Department said Monday.
In the annual Prospective Plantings report, USDA pegged wheat sowings at 69.187 million acres, including 3.185 million of durum wheat and 17.775 million of other spring wheat.
Cotton acreage was estimated at 14,484,500 acres.
The surge in corn and soybean plantings was far larger than expected. Cotton plantings also topped estimates. Soybean acres will be seven percent above 1996, and corn two percent above.
In 1996, farmers planted 64.2 million acres of soybeans, 79.5 million of corn, 75.6 million of wheat, 20.04 million of spring wheat other than durum, and 14.67 million of cotton.

A sizable wheat crop was possible despite smaller acreage, analysts said, because of high acreage abandonment in 1996. Corn acreage would be the highest since 83.398 million in 1985, and soybeans the highest since 69.930 million in 1980.
A companion report showed wheat, corn and soybean stocks to be lower than expected.
Indiana and Ohio were the only major soybean states where acreage would drop this year as land was rotated to corn.
USDA 1997 intended plantings of major crops for all purposes (Indicated 1997, Planted 1996, Percent of 1997/96).
The department revised 1997 winter wheat plantings from 48,222,000 acres reported on January 10.
The intended plantings estimates are based on reports from farmers.
